title: The Last Reel
hook: I run the projector at an old drive-in. One rule: if a car stays in the back row after the last movie, don't walk over to it.
lines: I run the projector at an old drive-in, out past the edge of town.
The owner had one rule. If a car stays in the back row after the last movie... don't walk over to it. Just shut down, and go home.
For three summers, every car left on time.
Then, on closing night, one stayed. Back row. Engine off. Windows fogged white.
I shut off the projector. The big screen went black.
There was no film in the machine. But the screen was showing the parking lot... filmed from that back row.
Nothing moved. Just moths, circling the speaker poles.
Then, on the screen, my booth door opened. And I watched myself walk out... across the gravel... toward that car.
But I hadn't moved. My hand was still on the switch.
On the screen, I climbed into that car... and everything went black.
I locked the booth until sunrise. At dawn, the car was gone. I went down to drive home.
My car wasn't where I'd parked it. It was in the back row now... windows fogged white. And someone in the driver's seat... was waving at me.
